title: Why You Must Join National Health Insurance Yourself
summary: Being a student is written into the law as a reason you cannot join your employer's scheme. So the bills come to you — and unpaid ones reach your visa renewal.
body_html:
Most students treat health insurance as optional until they need a doctor. It is not optional, you cannot get it through your part-time job, and unpaid premiums turn up in a place nobody warns you about.

The chain is short and every link is published.

Enrolment is not a choice

People living in Japan enrol in public medical insurance regardless of nationality. [source:1] The guidebook describes the purpose plainly: by sharing the burden across society as a whole, the system reduces the patient's own share of medical costs and guarantees equal access to good, advanced care. [source:1]

So the question is never whether you are in a scheme. It is which one.

Being a student is the reason you are excluded from the other one

There are two routes into public medical insurance, and one of them is closed to you by name.

Employees' health insurance covers people working at a company obliged to provide it — full-time staff, company representatives and officers, and part-timers working at least three quarters of the fixed weekly hours of a full-time employee at the same company. [source:1]

There is also a route for part-timers who meet a set of conditions together: a fixed weekly working time above a threshold, an expectation of being employed beyond a short initial period, monthly pay above a floor, employment at a company above a staff-count threshold — and, explicitly, being someone other than a student. [source:1]

Read that last condition again. Student status is not an incidental mismatch. It is written into the requirement as an exclusion.

The practical consequence: however many hours you work within your permit, and however large the employer, the part-timer route into employees' health insurance is not available to you as a student. You are in National Health Insurance, and nobody enrols you in it automatically.

Which means the bills come to you

Employees' health insurance premiums are, as a rule, split half and half between the company and the insured person. [source:1]

National Health Insurance has no employer on the other side of that split. The premium is billed to you, arrives on paper, and is easy to put in a drawer during a tight month.

That is the exact point at which a budgeting decision becomes an immigration one.

The part that reaches your visa

This is why the article exists, and it is not in any school's orientation.

The agency's guideline for changes of status and extensions of period of stay lists meeting your tax obligations among the considerations it weighs, and treats non-payment as a negative factor. [source:2] Beyond actual criminal penalty for non-payment, it states that large arrears or long-term arrears discovered without any penalty are treated the same way where the case is serious. [source:2]

Then the sentence that catches students: the same treatment applies to things you are required to pay by law such as National Health Insurance premiums, where large or long-term arrears come to light and the case is serious. [source:2]

National Health Insurance premiums are in the same paragraph as unpaid tax. A bill you ignored because it was not a tax is treated as though it were.

And the agency can find out. A note added in the June 2026 revision says it may decide taking into account information on your compliance obtained from relevant institutions at its request. [source:2]

What is also true, and is reassuring

Two things in the other direction, both official.

Since April 2010 the agency has asked applicants to present a health insurance card at the counter, to encourage enrolment — and since 2 December 2024, with the card discontinued, it asks instead for the My Number Portal eligibility information screen, the eligibility information notice, or an eligibility confirmation document. [source:2] It states plainly that being unable to present these will not result in refusal. [source:2]

So not having the document on you is not the problem. Not having paid is.

And the scheme you are in is a real one. The guidebook describes a high-cost medical expense benefit that pays back the amount above a monthly ceiling when what you paid at hospital or pharmacy windows exceeds it, with the final monthly ceiling depending on age and income level. [source:1] There is also a system for reimbursing costs you had to pay in full up front in defined situations, including treatment received abroad and doctor-prescribed casts and braces. [source:1]

These are not small benefits, and they are the reason the premium is not simply a tax on being foreign.

What to do

  • Enrol at the municipal office, at the same visit as your address registration if you can. You are going there anyway, and nobody will enrol you for you.
  • Do not wait for a job to sort it out. The part-timer route into employees' health insurance excludes students by name. [source:1]
  • Pay the bills, and keep the receipts. Arrears are weighed at renewal in the same breath as unpaid tax. [source:2]
  • If you cannot pay, go to the municipal office before the arrears build. Municipalities have reduction and deferral arrangements; we are not going to describe terms that differ by municipality, but the conversation exists and an unopened envelope is not it.
  • Do not panic about the card. Not being able to present it is explicitly not a ground for refusal. [source:2]

For the full set of considerations weighed at renewal — including the attendance item that matters more than any of this — see what immigration actually looks at when you renew. For the arrival paperwork this sits alongside, see your first week in Japan. For where the money comes from in the first place, see minimum wage by prefecture.

Premiums, thresholds and municipal arrangements differ by area and change; the guidebook reflects systems as at a stated date. The sources below are the authority. This page is a summary and not advice — if you are already in arrears, the municipal office is the place to go, not a forum.

claims_without_sources: 短時間労働者の加入要件の具体的な数値（週の所定労働時間・月額賃金・従業員数の各閾値）—— ガイドブックに記載があるが、この出典は約14万字の冊子であり、闸门の整页照合では2桁の数字が核対できない（ページ番号だけで小さい数字が揃う）。数値を書けば未核対の数字を本文に置くことになるため、「閾値がある」という形にとどめた。記事の論点は閾値の値ではなく「学生以外」という除外条項なので、これで成立する。
自己負担割合・高額療養費の上限額 —— 同じ理由で数値を書いていない。制度の存在と仕組みのみ述べた。
国民健康保険料の金額・算定方法 —— 自治体ごとに異なり、ガイドブックにも一律の額はない。
減免・分割納付の要件 —— 自治体の管轄で、出典にない。「制度があり窓口で相談できる」とだけ書き、条件は書いていない。
「高額」「長期」の未納がどの水準からそう扱われるか —— 入管庁は示していない。「悪質なものについては」という出典の表現に留めた。
住民登録と同時に国保加入手続ができるか —— 自治体によって運用が異なり、ガイドブックの当該箇所から確認していない。「できれば同じ来庁で」と書き、必ずできるとは述べていない。
